name: c-split-diptych
prompt: A tall portrait drawing in black india ink on creamy off-white newsprint, done in the manner of a hand-inked American newspaper cartoon from around 1919: confident tapering pen lines, dense cross-hatching for shadow, stippled grain on the ground, solid black only in hat, coat and shoe. The page is divided into two stacked panels of equal height, each framed by a thin, slightly wobbly hand-ruled ink border, with a clean blank white band about a sixth of the page tall running across the middle between them, empty of any marks. Top panel: a city park just after the Great War, bare elm branches, a gravel path and gas lamp drawn in fine hatching, a wrought-iron and slatted-wood bench seen straight on from chest height. On the left end of the bench sits a stout, round-bellied rich man with heavy jowls, a tall silk top hat, a black frock coat straining over a checked waistcoat with a gold watch chain, spats, one gloved hand lifted palm-out in a lazy brush-off gesture, eyes half-closed, chin raised. Beside him on the right a gaunt young soldier in a rumpled khaki tunic and puttees, one trouser leg pinned up empty below the knee, a wooden crutch across his lap, cap in his hands, looking at the man. Bottom panel: the same bench in the same spot and the same camera height, but the park around it is today, a litter bin, a lamp post with an LED head, a glass office block behind the trees, all in the identical pen-and-hatch technique. The rich man is an exact repeat of the top panel: same position on the left end of the bench, same size, same angle, same raised gloved hand, same half-closed eyes, same coat folds and same top hat, so that he sits directly beneath himself like a rubber stamp printed twice. Beside him on the right now sits a worn-out nurse in loose scrubs with a lanyard and soft clogs, hair coming loose, shoulders slumped, a paper cup in both hands, looking at him. Everything around the man changes between the panels; he does not change in any line. Even, flat daylight in both panels, no colour at all, only black ink on warm cream paper, faint paper fibre and slight ink bleed at line edges. No words, letters, signatures, captions or speech balloons anywhere in the image.
